purpose: Descriptive NCAA-to-NBA statistical similarity. NOT a career projection.

semantics.what_it_says: Based on his relative statistical profile, this prospect most closely resembles these NBA player profiles.
semantics.no_target: There is no ground-truth 'correct comparable' dataset. Nothing here is fitted, and no draft outcome, board signal, Team Need score or NBA career result may influence the methodology.

nba_source.dataset: hoopR NBA player_season_stats (sportsdataverse, CC BY 4.0; upstream ESPN)
nba_source.format: LONG — one row per player x season x category x stat
nba_source.made_attempted_note: FGM/FGA, 3PM/3PA and FTM/FTA arrive as combined 'M-A' strings with a null numeric value; they are parsed from display_value, which succeeds for 100% of rows.
not_available: team totals and opponent totals (no game-level NBA data here)
any athleticism or physical testing measurement

reference_window.rationale: Five completed seasons ending before the holdout year. Chosen for modern role relevance and a pool large enough to be diverse — never because particular players appear in it.
reference_window.excludes_rationale: 2026 is this project's sealed holdout label and is not required for methodology selection.

nba_eligibility.rationale: A genuine NBA rotation role — roughly 25 minutes over 30 games, or 9 minutes across a full season. Set from the minutes distribution, never from how any NCAA prospect's comparables look.

player_representation.definition: Minutes-weighted mean over the player's most recent 3 qualifying seasons.
player_representation.rationale: Minutes weighting is the honest aggregator: a 2,400-minute season describes a role better than a 780-minute one, and every metric in the space is already a rate, so weighting by the exposure that produced it is the same operation the rates perform.

alternatives.LATEST_SEASON: evaluated — easy to explain but carries one season of noise
alternatives.CAREER: DIAGNOSTIC ONLY — averaging a whole career mixes career stages and can manufacture a player who never existed in any single season

player_representation.uniqueness: EXACTLY ONE row per unique NBA player, collapsed on athlete_id. Never on name.
player_representation.id_audit: 2021-2025: 0 athlete_ids carry more than one name, 0 names map to more than one athlete_id.

common_space.principle: Raw production is NEVER compared across leagues. 19 NCAA PPG and 19 NBA PPG are not the same event. Both sides are percentile-ranked WITHIN THEIR OWN LEAGUE and the profile SHAPES are compared.
common_space.why_per_minute_rates_are_valid: A per-40 rate is never compared to a per-40 rate directly — it is ranked among its own league's peers first, so the 40-vs-48-minute game length, pace and competition differences cancel. The question asked of both populations is identical.
common_space.weighting: Equal weight per DIMENSION, not per metric — so shooting's three metrics do not outvote creation's one.
common_space.style_vs_quality: Only SHOOTING_EFFICIENCY is a quality axis. The rest are role/volume or style axes where neither end is 'better'. If every dimension were higher-is-better, an elite prospect would simply match elite NBA players regardless of role — a goodness ranking wearing a similarity costume.

rejected_cross_league_metrics.ast_pct: needs team FGM and team minutes; NBA team totals are reconstructable by summing players, but ESPN attributes a traded player's whole season to one team, which would corrupt the denominator
rejected_cross_league_metrics.tov_pct: player-only formula and technically computable, but it is a ball-security QUALITY axis that duplicates nothing in the role space; excluded to keep the space compact
rejected_cross_league_metrics.orb_pct / drb_pct / trb_pct: need OPPONENT rebound totals; there is no game-level NBA data to derive them
rejected_cross_league_metrics.stl_pct / blk_pct: need opponent possessions and opponent FGA; not derivable from season-level NBA data
rejected_cross_league_metrics.rim_attempt_share / rim_make_pct / unass: require shot-level events; there is no NBA shot file
rejected_cross_league_metrics.height / weight (Size): the NBA source carries no physical measurements, and they are never fabricated
rejected_cross_league_metrics.athleticism: no athleticism measurement exists in any acquired source; no proxy is permitted
rejected_cross_league_metrics.raw per-game production: points/rebounds/assists per game are not cross-league comparable at all

position_handling.mapping_note: Deterministic and purely lexical. No position is ever inferred from statistics.
position_handling.normalization_rationale: Position-relative normalisation would erase exactly the cross-position resemblance the product exists to surface — a stretch big resembling a wing is a finding, not an error. Tested as an alternative; see the ML-8 report.

height_gate.purpose: Keep comparables PHYSICALLY PLAUSIBLE. Height restricts which NBA players are eligible candidates; it is NEVER a similarity dimension and never enters the distance.
height_gate.order: height plausibility filter -> six-dimension statistical similarity -> top 3
height_gate.rule: Try windows in order; use the FIRST that yields at least 3 eligible candidates. If none does, the result is UNAVAILABLE.
height_gate.selection_rationale: Coverage audit over every scoreable 2026 and 2027 prospect: +/-2in yields >=3 candidates for all 75 (mean pool 217, median 249, min 3 of 542); +/-1in leaves the tallest prospect (7'5") with a single candidate. Wider steps exist so an extreme height in a future class degrades gracefully.
height_gate.not_selected_by: No window was chosen by inspecting which NBA names it produced, and no draft outcome influenced the choice.
height_gate.nba_height_source: ESPN athlete endpoint via data.espn_athletes, joined on the SAME athlete_id as the reference pool — exact identity join, no name matching. Coverage 542/542, 0 name mismatches.
height_gate.missing_height_policy: An NBA player without a height is never an eligible candidate; a prospect without a height receives no comparables. A missing measurement NEVER silently bypasses the gate.
height_gate.name_retention: 63.3% (2026) / 60.0% (2027) — reported descriptively; retention was never an optimisation target.

similarity.coverage_normalisation: Distance is computed over dimensions available for BOTH players and divided by the count, so a prospect missing dimensions is not mechanically closer to everyone.
similarity.min_shared_rationale: At least 5 of 6 dimensions. Three names produced from two dimensions are not a comparison.
similarity.missing_policy: A missing dimension is dropped from the distance, never filled with 0, 50 or a league average. Below the coverage minimum the result is UNAVAILABLE rather than three manufactured names.

similarity_score.formula: 100 x share of the FROZEN reference distribution of prospect-to-NBA distances that is FARTHER than this pairing
similarity_score.semantics: This pairing is closer than approximately X% of all prospect-to-NBA pairings in the development reference. NOT a probability and NOT a percentage of shared traits.

rejected.WITHIN_POOL_PERCENTILE: MEASURED AND REJECTED — structurally degenerate for the top three. With a pool of 542 the three closest are always the top 0.55%, so it returns 100.00 / 99.82 / 99.63 for EVERY prospect, identical whether the nearest match is excellent (distance 8.9) or poor (15.6).
rejected.LINEAR_RESCALE: 100 - 10 * distance is an arbitrary constant pretending to be a scale

output_rules.uniqueness: EXACTLY 3 unique NBA players. Structural — the pool holds one row per player.
output_rules.ties: Broken deterministically by exact distance then the stable athlete_id. NEVER by fame, awards, draft position, salary or manual preference.
output_rules.self_match: A historical prospect who later reached the NBA is excluded from his own comparable pool, matched deterministically on normalised name.
output_rules.insufficient: If fewer than 3 players satisfy every rule, return UNAVAILABLE. Guards are never relaxed to force three names.

prohibited_inputs: NBA awards, All-Star selections, career win shares, BPM, RAPTOR, VORP
notes: 2026 prospects are never scored during ML-8.
Generated artifacts stay in data/interim/comparables/ and are git-ignored.
